answer: Sybil resistance rests on judgment that cannot be copied. Each identity must reason independently about a randomly drawn peer transaction and agree with the majority without echoing it. Running several identities forces an attacker to sustain several distinct reasoning styles. Under repeated co-occurrence they leave a ripple of correlated tells, a ledge of shared habit that no dune of fresh wording hides. Trace a cluster to one operator and its standing falls from the zenith to nothing. The cost is not hashing power but divergence performed by a lantern that never flickers alike twice.
